item.title: Lelean break northern hearts
item.description: LELEAN Memorial School broke northern hearts but created their own piece of glory after edging Navatu Secondary School 15-14 in a pulsating Vodafone Super Deans under-19 final at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva yesterday. For Navatu, it was a cruel end to a remarkable campaign.
item.content:encoded:
LELEAN Memorial School broke northern hearts but created their own piece of glory after edging Navatu Secondary School 15-14 in a pulsating Vodafone Super Deans under-19 final at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva yesterday.

For Navatu, it was a cruel end to a remarkable campaign.

The northern champions had arrived at the final with history within reach as the first school from the North to contest a Vodafone Super Deans final, but a missed penalty with the final act of the match denied them a fairytale finish.

Navatu came out firing, dominating territory and pinning Lelean deep inside their own red zone for much of the opening half.

Their exceptional handling, willingness to shift the ball and expansive running game troubled the Davuilevu side as they crossed for two converted tries to establish a 14-0 lead.

They stayed composed, tightened their discipline and gradually worked their way back into the contest, scoring a try and adding a penalty to cut the deficit to 14-8 at halftime.

The Davuilevu side lifted the tempo and eventually crossed for a converted try to take a 15-14 lead for the first time in the match.

From there, their well-organised defence and improved discipline proved decisive as they kept the desperate Navatu attack at bay and forced their northern opponents into costly errors and penalties.

Navatu were handed one final opportunity when awarded a penalty in the dying moments, but the kick failed to find its target, sparking wild celebrations among the Lelean players and supporters.

Lelean head coach Peni Vakatawakoula said his side had prepared for the physical and fast-paced challenge Navatu brought.

“The boys stuck to the game plan and it paid off in the end,” he said.

“We had anticipated a tough match against Navatu and they did just that, but the message to the boys was to trust our processes. They did just that and the result speaks for itself.”

For Navatu captain and number eight Vilimone Kanawabu, the defeat was difficult to accept.

“That was a really close game that we should have won. The pressure and our mistakes cost us the match,” he said.

“I still can’t believe we let that match slip.”

Yet, despite the heartbreak, Kanawabu urged northern schools not to lose belief.

“For so long we have doubted ourselves in the North, but my message to all the players and teams back in the North is that anything is possible. The secret is faith and hard work.”

For Vakatawakoula, the victory belonged to more than just the 23 players who took the field.

He dedicated the title to the school, its old scholars, loyal supporters and the players’ families, whom he described as the pillars behind the team’s journey throughout the season.

item.title: Maroons edge Rewa in Round 4
item.description: KHELVIN Civil Engineering Lautoka Maroons secured their first win of the Skipper Cup season with a 28-23 victory over FMF Rewa Senior Men’s in Round Four at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday. Head coach Kiniviliame Bavadra praised his players for showing resilience and intensity on the field.
item.content:encoded:
KHELVIN Civil Engineering Lautoka Maroons secured their first win of the Skipper Cup season with a 28-23 victory over FMF Rewa Senior Men’s in Round Four at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday.

Head coach Kiniviliame Bavadra praised his players for showing resilience and intensity on the field.

After suffering defeats in their opening three matches, the Maroons finally broke through against Rewa, holding their nerve despite playing with only 12 men on the field.

Bavadra described the victory as a major boost for his side and a sign that the team is prepared to fight until the final whistle.

“I would say it’s a big green light for us in terms of staying in the fight and fighting until the end of the game,” Bavadra said.

However, the coach acknowledged that discipline remains an area the Maroons must improve after three yellow cards were issued to his players in the second half.

Bavadra said the problem was not simply discipline but also the players’ mindset and decision-making in crucial areas of the game.

“It can’t be just discipline alone but mindset in terms of how we want to engage in certain areas where we are already ;acking,” he said.

He said the team had discussed the breakdown during the halftime break and attempted to add numbers, but some players were penalised for cynical play.

“It’s really unnecessary and it goes back to how we prepare ourselves,” Bavadra said.

Following three consecutive losses, Bavadra said the message to his players was simple — continue grinding and find a way to win.

“The message is just to grind and get the win in a way that we haven’t showed or displayed in the previous three games,” he said.

The coach was particularly pleased with the intensity his players maintained throughout the match.

What I’m happy with was the intensity. We stayed in the game,” he said.

“We’ve been missing those for the first three games and I’m happy with the way they ended the match to get the win 28-23 against Rewa.”

We dedicated the win to the vanua, players families, supporters and fans of the Lautoka Maroons.

item.title: Tavua College shine
item.description: Western schools finished the Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship on top, claiming four titles across the major grades. The final piece of the Western success came when Tavua College defeated Labasa College 2-0 in the U19 final, the last match of the championship.
item.content:encoded:
Western schools finished the Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship on top, claiming four titles across the major grades.

The final piece of the Western success came when Tavua College defeated Labasa College 2-0 in the U19 final, the last match of the championship.

Tavua’s victory followed title-winning performances from other Western schools across the tournament.

Lautoka Central College won the U15 title after edging AD Patel College 1-0, while Ba Sangam College secured the U17 crown with a 4-1 victory over Labasa Muslim College.

Tavua also claimed the open-grade girls title, adding to its successful campaign.

The results highlighted the strength and depth of school football in the Western Division, with schools producing champions across the age groups and the open-grade girls competition.

The U19 final provided a fitting finish to the championship, with Tavua College completing the Western schools’ strong showing with a two-goal victory over Labasa College.

The four titles capped an impressive tournament for Western schools, which returned home with the major honours across the championship’s key grades.

item.title: Saint John’s Cawaci celebrate double hockey triumph
item.description: SAINT John’s College Cawaci has been crowned the Girls Overall Champion of the Fiji Secondary Schools Hockey Tournament after winning both the Under-16 and Under-19 girls titles at Nadovu Hockey Ground in Lautoka yesterday. The achievement sparked celebrations among the Cawaci team, with Under-16 team manager Lusiana Hawili dedicating the success to God and acknowledging the unwavering support of
item.content:encoded:
SAINT John’s College Cawaci has been crowned the Girls Overall Champion of the Fiji Secondary Schools Hockey Tournament after winning both the Under-16 and Under-19 girls titles at Nadovu Hockey Ground in Lautoka yesterday.

The achievement sparked celebrations among the Cawaci team, with Under-16 team manager Lusiana Hawili dedicating the success to God and acknowledging the unwavering support of parents, former students and supporters.

Hawili said the journey from Ovalau had not been easy, but the team remained determined throughout the tournament.

“I would like to give all the glory and thanks to Almighty God for giving us the strength for this journey. It wasn’t an easy journey coming all the way from Ovalau,” Hawili said.

She also praised the parents, ex-scholars and supporters who continued to rally behind the players throughout the competition.

“We would like to thank them for all their support rendered to the girls and the boys,” she said.

Hawili said the team was overwhelmed with joy after securing both girls titles and bringing the trophies back to Ovalau.

“We are just overwhelmed to be taking back both the Under-16 and Under-19 girls back to Ovalau. It’s a celebration here and we are just so happy. Our joy cannot be explained,” she said.

The double triumph marks a memorable campaign for Cawaci, with the school proving its strength across both age grades to claim the overall girl’s championship.

Meanwhile, in the boy’s division, Tilak High School defeated Marist Brothers High School 2-1 in the Under-16 final while MBHS Under-19 boys secured a well-earned 1-0 victory over Dilkusha Methodist High School.

item.title: Grammar wins after 21 years
item.description: AFTER a 21-year wait, the Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Vodafone Super Deans under-18 title has triumphantly returned to Nasese. In a masterful showcase of forward dominance, structured teamwork and an unyielding Lions spirit, Suva Grammar School roared to a commanding 36-21 victory over a determined Lelean Memorial School side at HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva yesterday.
item.content:encoded:
AFTER a 21-year wait, the Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Vodafone Super Deans under-18 title has triumphantly returned to Nasese.

In a masterful showcase of forward dominance, structured teamwork and an unyielding Lions spirit, Suva Grammar School roared to a commanding 36-21 victory over a determined Lelean Memorial School side at HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva yesterday.

The SGS forwards provided the backbone of the victory, relentlessly winning collisions and taking control of the set pieces.

Their powerful rolling maul produced the opening try and immediately set the tone for a final in which the Grammarians applied pressure from the opening whistle to the last.

Head coach Epeli Osbourne paid tribute to his players for delivering the relentless performance they had worked towards.

“I thought the boys were outstanding. Outstanding,” Osbourne said.

“Relentless pressure is what we wanted from the first minute to the last, and they gave us that. I take my hat off to the boys. They’re the ones who did the work.”

Despite LMS fighting back and refusing to surrender, the young Lions held firm, trusting their structures and responding whenever the Dauvilevu side threatened.

Osbourne said the halftime message was simple, maintain the pressure, remain alert and play to the conditions.

“We just wanted to keep that same pressure on and stay on our guard,” he said.

“Keep it simple, play to the conditions, just like we told them back in school before we came here.”

Grammar entered the final with confidence in its ability to challenge LMS at the set piece, an area Osbourne believed would be crucial to the outcome.

“We knew our stats. We knew what we were capable of and we just wanted to perfect that,” he said.

“We were quietly confident that we were going to come and dominate that set piece. Without a set piece, you can’t launch.”

For Osbourne, who had previously experienced the Deans competition as a Grammar player, yesterday’s victory carried special significance.

“I’ve been telling these boys ever since we’ve been coming, right from under-14, I’m sick and tired of talking to under-18s every year,” he said.

“So we talked about it as a group, and I told them, ‘I’ll jump in and we’ll try to show the boys in Grammar how it’s done.’”

Osbourne also credited the Grammar community for its unwavering support throughout the campaign.

“All the scholars and the support of the Grammar community have been awesome. We wouldn’t be doing this without their support,” he said.

The Grammar faithful turned out in huge numbers to support all three school teams competing in the finals, with the U18 victory providing a fitting reward for their loyalty.

After 21 years, the Lions have finally reclaimed their place at the top.

item.title: Lautoka breaks losing streak
item.description: THE Khelvin Civil Engineering Lautoka Women’s team has bounced back in style, securing an impressive victory over Rewa 51-30 in Round Four of the Subrails Marama Cup competition at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday. Team manager Litiana Koroibola said the win was a proud moment for the Lautoka side after suffering defeats to Nadi, Nadroga and Naitasiri in their opening three matches.
item.content:encoded:
THE Khelvin Civil Engineering Lautoka Women’s team has bounced back in style, securing an impressive victory over Rewa 51-30 in Round Four of the Subrails Marama Cup competition at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday.

Team manager Litiana Koroibola said the win was a proud moment for the Lautoka side after suffering defeats to Nadi, Nadroga and Naitasiri in their opening three matches.

“We won this home game, and I am proud of the girls for their performance today in getting us a win,” Koroibola said.

The victory was also a reward for the hard work put in by the team management, which has faced challenges in rebuilding the squad after several players moved to other rugby unions. Koroibola, who is in her fourth year as team manager, said recruiting players had been difficult task, prompting the appointment of Alena Laqai as head coach.

Laqai brought in four players from Jasper Williams High School Raluve Under-18 team who made an impact in the Round Four clash.

Despite the three earlier losses, Koroibola said the team never lost faith in its players and believed they could improve as the competition continued.

She acknowledged that there were still areas to work on, particularly discipline, despite the positive result against Rewa.

Lautoka now turns its attention to next week’s challenging assignment against Kadavu, where the Maroons women will travel to Namalata District School ground.

“We will give our best and we will work on our weaknesses,” Koroibola said.

She also issued a special invitation to Lautoka supporters living in Kadavu to come out in numbers.

Koroibola thanked God and the team’s sponsors, BLK and Khelvin Civil Engineering, for their continued support of women’s rugby in Lautoka.

With their first win secured, the Lautoka women will now look to build momentum and make their next outing in Kadavu as another step forward.

item.title: Cawaci draws rugby strength into hockey challenge
item.description: SAINT John’s College Cawaci is confident of making a strong challenge for the hockey title, with the school’s boys’ team drawing on the fitness and experience of players who have recently completed the rugby season. Cawaci competes in the Fiji Secondary Schools Hockey Championships with four teams, featuring the Under-16 girls and boys and Under-19 girls and boys’ categories.
item.content:encoded:
SAINT John’s College Cawaci is confident of making a strong challenge for the hockey title, with the school’s boys’ team drawing on the fitness and experience of players who have recently completed the rugby season.

Cawaci competes in the Fiji Secondary Schools Hockey Championships with four teams, featuring the Under-16 girls and boys and Under-19 girls and boys’ categories.

School teacher Lusiana Hawili said the transition from rugby to hockey had been relatively smooth for the boys, with most of the players already fit and accustomed to playing hockey.

“Most of our boys, since there are fewer numbers in our team, are from the Under-18s. Our preparation was good because since they transitioned from rugby to hockey, they were already fit,” Hawili said.

She said the main areas of focus for the team would be its defence and execution of short corners.

“We need to focus on our defence. We must be careful with our defence and our short corners. Other than that, I have a good feeling we’ll take back something to Cawaci”

Cawaci’s Under-19 boys reached the final last year but went down to Levuka Public School.

Hawili said that defeat had motivated the players to go one step further this year.

“We reached the finals and we lost to LPS. We are just encouraging the boys that we can win this year,” she said.

She added that many of the players had been involved in hockey since Under-16 level while also playing rugby, making the transition between the two sports easier.

“Most of them have been playing hockey from Under-16 and they are also joining the rugby team. After the rugby season, they always come and join.”

Hawili also believes hockey continues to develop strongly in Ovalau, despite being regarded as a minor sport in Fiji.

She said all three schools on the island are involved in hockey, with the sport also being passed down through families.

“It has been developing very well because in Ovalau, most of all the three schools, St John’s College, Levuka Public School and Delana Methodist High School Levuka, they all play hockey,” she said.

“Most of the students that are playing hockey right now, their parents used to be hockey reps, and they have that urge in them to also play hockey.”

However, Hawili said Cawaci still needed to work on its weaknesses, particularly in defence, to continue improving.

For the girls, her main hope is for the players to enjoy the sport while also challenging for silverware.

“I would just love for them to enjoy the sport and also love for us to take back the trophy since it has been so long,” she said.

Cawaci last lifted the trophy in 2024 after beating Saint Thomas High School 1-nil in the final but fell short in the final last year against Levuka Public School, making this year’s campaign an opportunity to end a wait for success.
